body_markdown:
Ford traveled to SEMA 2026 to unveil a new, supercharged crate engine called Megazilla 2.0. Instead of merely putting the huge, 7.3-liter V-8 on display in the middle of its booth, it stuffed it into a one-off, heavily modified Bronco called the Ford Frostwarden.


The main difference between the original Megazilla and the Megazilla 2.0 is that the former is naturally aspirated while the latter is fitted with a 3.0-liter Gen 6 Whipple supercharger. However, Ford stresses that adding forced induction to the V-8 required several changes. It developed a stronger engine block to handle the extra power, a supercharger-specific camshaft, and upgraded pistons. Larger injectors spray more fuel into the cylinders, while the belt drive and damper were also designed for the new V-8.


All told, the Megazilla 2.0 makes over 1200 horsepower and 1000 pound-feet of torque when burning race fuel, figures normally found in the supercar segment. These numbers represent a massive increase over the naturally aspirated Megazilla, which makes 615 horsepower and 670 pound-feet of torque. Ford claims that the 2.0 is the most powerful crate engine ever created by a carmaker.

Tall, wide, and muscular-looking, the Frostwarden concept is as wild as the engine that powers it. It’s based on a four-door Bronco, and Ford envisioned it as a vehicle that would feel right at home in an Arctic search-and-rescue team’s fleet. The company added Dana parts in the driveline, 74Weld-sourced portal axles, and custom Bilstein dampers to increase off-road capability. Ford also fitted wheel arch flares to enable 18-inch Weld beadlock wheels wrapped in 42-inch tires. Accessories like a winch, a light bar, and tailgate-mounted fuel cans round out the modifications. The result is a Bronco that looks capable of tackling any terrain.


While it’s undeniably cool, the Ford Frostwarden is a concept built for SEMA rather than a preview of a new trim. The good news is that it uses many off-the-shelf parts, so you can build one just like it if you have enough time, money, and fabrication skills.


As for the Megazilla 2.0, it’s headed to Ford’s catalog of crate engines in the near future. Pricing hasn’t been released, but nothing suggests that it will be cheap. For context, the naturally aspirated Megazilla V-8[remains available](https://performanceparts.ford.com/part/M-6007-MZ73) with a base price of $25,295.
